eyebrow: Why Compose stops at one host
code:
# Compose assumes every service lives on ONE machine:
#   - one shared default network (Lesson 24)
#   - named volumes tied to that host's disk
#   - depends_on, scoped to containers on this host
#
# There is no `docker compose` flag that spreads
# catalog, api, and db across a second server, or
# that notices when the host itself goes down.
caption: Compose manages containers on one host well -- it was never designed to manage hosts.

code:
Docker Swarm      -- Docker's own orchestrator; turns a
                     compose.yaml deploy: block into a real
                     multi-host deployment. Simple, less used
                     in production than the option below.

Kubernetes (k8s)  -- the industry-standard orchestrator.
                     Same ideas as Swarm, its own YAML shapes
                     (Pods, Deployments, Services), and a much
                     larger ecosystem. What most teams run.
caption: Same containers you already built -- the orchestrator just decides where they run.
